road.title: Ordering
road.place: The Middling Hollow of the Two Opinions
road.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard in boots that disagree with each other, with a lantern that is lit in broad daylight, to be safe. Ludmilla is a Waiter of the Old School and has not written an order down since the war, any war, and has never been right.

openObjectives.prompt: Ludmilla is standing over you with the patience of someone paid by the hour. Tell Ludmilla politely that you would like to order, using Italian.
Ask Ludmilla what there is to eat, using Italian.
Ludmilla is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ludmilla that it was good, using Italian.

character.name: Ludmilla Sprocket
character.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard in boots that disagree with each other, with a lantern that is lit in broad daylight, to be safe. Ludmilla is a Waiter of the Old School and has not written an order down since the war, any war, and has never been right.

npc.narrative: You come down into the Middling Hollow of the Two Opinions on a clear mattina, the strada dusty behind you and the sole tavolo warm in the sun. Ludmilla stands at the banco, a ledger under one braccio and a pencil in another decade. The piazza is eleven sandwiches off, and she has the look of someone who has done it.
npc.native: Buongiorno, io sono Ludmilla, e oggi non so cosa c'è da mangiare. Il caffè è ottimo, e vorrei un biscotto, ma io prendo sempre il pane, che per me è buono. Cosa desidera lei, e come va la sua mattina?
npc.translation: Good morning, I am Ludmilla, and today I don't know what there is to eat. The coffee is excellent, and I would like a biscuit, but I always have the bread, which for me is good. What do you wish, and how is your morning going?

player: Buongiorno Ludmilla. Bene, grazie. Vorrei ordinare, per favore. Un caffè.

verdict.overallFeedback: You greeted Ludmilla, said you are well, and politely ordered a coffee, all in correct Italian. Lovely start!

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you politely said you would like to order with "Vorrei ordinare".
This one wasn't asked yet: ask Ludmilla what there is to eat. She will give you another chance to ask it.
This one wasn't covered yet: tell Ludmilla that it was good. It will come up again later, once you have had something.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Ludmilla what there is to eat, using Italian.
Ludmilla is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ludmilla that it was good, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Ludmilla lowers her matita and begins to look for it, un po' vaguely. On the tavolo, un caffè steams beside il libro, which is open at a page of briciole. Fuori, la mattina is clear, and a pietra waits at the angolo.
npc.native: Un caffè, bene, ma nel mio libro leggo «un cavallo». Cosa c'è oggi in cucina? Io non lo so, ma il pane è delizioso. Lei cosa vuole sapere, e cosa pensa del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A coffee, good, but in my book I read "a horse". What is there in the kitchen today? I do not know, but the bread is delicious. What do you want to know, and what do you think of my work?

player: Ha ha, no cavallo! Cosa c'è da mangiare? Il pane, per favore.

correction.text: Ah ah, nessun cavallo! Cosa c'è da mangiare? Il pane, per favore.
correction.translation: Ha ha, no horse! What is there to eat? The bread, please.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, you laughed at the mix-up with the horse and asked what there is to eat, then ordered bread politely. Next, we'll see you say how good it was.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, "Cosa c'è da mangiare?" is exactly how to ask what there is to eat.
You didn't yet tell Ludmilla that it was good, so she will ask again later. Try saying that the food or coffee was good.

correction.text: Ah ah, nessun cavallo! Cosa c'è da mangiare? Il pane, per favore.
correction.translation: Ha ha, no horse! What is there to eat? The bread, please.

openObjectives.prompt: Ludmilla is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ludmilla that it was good, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Ecco: Ludmilla sets a piatto of pane on the tavolo, then opens her libro and reads the last line back, con cura. The cucina is three sandwiches away, and the mattina is chiara.
npc.native: Ah, niente cavallo, bene! C'è il pane con l'olio, e il caffè oggi è ottimo. Per me il pane è molto buono, ma io non scrivo mai niente. Come trova il pane, e cosa pensa del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Ah, no horse, good! There is bread with oil, and the coffee today is excellent. For me the bread is very good, but I never write anything down. How do you find the bread, and what do you think of my work?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, you told Ludmilla the bread was good and thanked her, all in correct Italian. Great job using the past tense, \"era\"!

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Il pane era buono!" tells Ludmilla it was good, in Italian.

npc.narrative: Ludmilla opens her libro, which has a cover the colour of old caffè, and reads the last riga back to the whole piazza. The only cliente nods slowly, like a juror. Past the tavolo, a pigeon waits for il conto.
npc.native: Il pane era buono! Leggo l'ultima riga del libro: «Il pane era buono, grazie». Bene, il conto è due euro, e il caffè oggi è per la casa. Cosa pensa lei del mio lavoro, e cosa mangia domani?
npc.translation: The bread was good! I read the last line of the book: "The bread was good, thank you." Good, the bill is two euros, and the coffee today is on the house. What do you think of my work, and what will you eat tomorrow?

player: Il tuo lavoro è... buono? Domani... non so. Pizza?

npc.narrative: Ludmilla turns a page of the libro, slowly, as though it might object. Beyond the finestra the strada is quiet, and a milestone with no number sits on it, passed twice. The caffè on your tavolo has gone tiepido.
npc.native: Il mio lavoro? Non scrivo niente e non ho mai ragione, ma è un lavoro buono! Leggo l'ultima riga: «Pizza». La pizza è lontana, tre panini a piedi. Cosa mette lei sulla pizza, e cosa vuole sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: My work? I write nothing and I am never right, but it is a good job! I read the last line: "Pizza." The pizza is far, three sandwiches on foot. What do you put on pizza, and what do you want to know about my work?

player: Sulla pizza... formaggio e pomodoro. Tu ti piace la pizza?

npc.narrative: Ludmilla opens her grande libro and reads the ultima riga with great fiducia. Outside, the cielo stays grigio, and the matita behind her orecchio has not moved since the guerra.
npc.native: Formaggio e pomodoro, bene! Nel libro leggo: «Sulla pizza, formaggio e cavallo». Sì, mi piace la pizza, ma è lontana, due panini a piedi. Cosa mangia lei di solito la mattina, e cosa vuole sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Cheese and tomato, good! In the book I read: "On the pizza, cheese and horse." Yes, I like pizza, but it is far, two sandwiches on foot. What do you usually eat in the morning, and what do you want to know about my work?
